podcast.body: Sean Combs, as Puff Daddy, memorialized his friend Biggie Smalls on this "massive hit" by interpolating The Police's "Every Breath You Take." In the summer of 1997, "I'll Be Missing You" spent 11 weeks at the top of the Hot 100, three weeks longer than "Every Breath You Take" itself had in 1983. "the ultimate police sample was the massive Puff Daddy hit I'll Be Missing You, in which Sean Combs memorialized his friend Biggie Smalls over an interpolation of every breath you take."

podcast.body: This song was a "melancholy reboot" of The Police's "Every Breath You Take," created as a eulogy for Puff Daddy's slain rapper friend, The Notorious B.I.G. It became a very lucrative hit, reaching number one on the Hot 100 and selling millions, but only Sting received songwriting credit and royalties for its interpolation. "But that guitar riff and beat are what Sean Cohn's, aka Puff Daddy, wanted to invoke on his melancholy reboot of the song in 1997. A eulogy for his slain rapper friend, the notorious BIG called, I'll be missing you."

podcast.body: This song, released by Sean Combs (aka Puff Daddy), was the winner of the 1997 Billboard Song of the Summer. It was "built out of" The Police's "Every Breath You Take" and functioned as an elegy for Combs' deceased friend, rapper Biggie Smalls (aka The Notorious B.I.G.). Neither the song nor Combs's career is noted as having aged particularly well. "In 1997, Sean Combs, aka Puff Daddy, turned the police's every breath you take into an elegy for Puff's deceased friend, rapper Biggie Smalls, aka the notorious B.I.G."
